method.decompression: ezQuake cl_demo.c:2988 invocation `qizmo -q -u -3 -D <file.qwz>` via bundled 32-bit qizmo 2.91 + own loader/libs (no i386 multiarch). CWD holds compress.dat.
method.decision_rule: self_pov if move_active_frac>=0.45 AND move_nonzero_frac>=0.55; spectator if move_nonzero_frac<0.20; else ambiguous; too_short if <100 frames
method.calibration: self-POV samples (paradoks, etc) show move_nonzero_frac 0.82-0.86; autotrack/commentary samples show EXACTLY 0.00 — binary separation, no overlap

strength_cross_reference.rating_source: fantasyquake/data/individual_ratings.json (rate_individual.py, carry-corrected blended individual+team, openskill PlackettLuce)
strength_cross_reference.registry_era: 2024-2026 modern competitive — does NOT cover most classic-era (2003-2008) challenge-tv names
strength_cross_reference.interpretation: Strength match is REGISTRY-COVERAGE-LIMITED not strength-limited: the corpus is classic-era so most names predate the modern rating window. The matches that DO exist are high-strength Div1 (reppie #3 modern, ParadokS). The corpus's top-count players (crit, exile, wart, akke, spice, vana, janus) were era-elite. To rank classic players by per-skill DM3 signature, rate_individual.py would need to be re-run over the classic SmackDown MVD set (out of spike-3 scope).

infeasibility_floor.floor_definition_docs12: if < N self-POV 4on4 demos survive -> abandon learned MOVE/AIM-of-elites, fall back to hand controllers + stock combat
infeasibility_floor.yield_vs_floor: 472 self-POV 4on4 match demos / 37.56M ground-truth usercmd frames / 256 distinct players / 443 full-match-length
infeasibility_floor.comparator_MLMove: MLMove (SIGGRAPH SCA 2024) behaviourally-cloned pro CS team movement from 123h of play. 37.56M frames at ~72Hz ~= 145 hours of self-POV input — same order of magnitude as MLMove's training set, for a SINGLE map.
infeasibility_floor.rationale: The feared 'no elite DM3 POV corpus' is decisively false. Self-POV match-demo yield exceeds any reasonable floor by ~2 orders of magnitude (472 vs a plausible N=10-25). Frame volume (~145h) is comparable to the published MLMove BC corpus on one map. Learned MOVE and aim-tracking-dynamics BC are data-feasible. CAVEATS that scope the claim: (1) per-player depth is thin for BC of a SINGLE elite's signature (max 10 demos/player; most have 1-2) — pretraining on the pooled corpus + ztricks prior, then per-player fine-tune, is the realistic shape, not 'clone one player from their demos alone'; (2) AIM target-selection still needs POV x MVD fusion (per-frame opponent positions) which this census does not provide — only aim-tracking DYNAMICS are feasible from POV alone, exactly as docs/12 §5 already states; (3) classic-era strength ranking needs rate_individual.py re-run over SmackDown MVDs to pick clone targets by per-skill signature.
